goal: Build a tcgen05 Blackwell GEMM with ThunderKittens and measure whether it beats the shipped vendor trailing GEMM (cuBLAS TF32 / MXFP8) on this campaign's large-n shapes. Closes levers.md lever #3.
promotion_policy: adopt only if BOTH public and secret splits improve
completed_gates: toolchain: TK 2.0 compiles via load_inline on cuda13-devel + torch 2.13.0+cu130 at sm_100a (fixes: qualify kittens::detail::tcgen05::commit; extra_ldflags -lcuda -lcudadevrt for the driver API)
correctness: tcgen05 GEMM rel_err 0.2-0.3% vs fp32 on all 4 shapes
benchmark B200: TK 293 TFLOPs @4096^3 (= TK's published level_06 number); 0.19-0.56x cuBLAS on every shape

result.kernel: TK educational_b200/level_06 class (naive tcgen05 + TMA), generalized to M,N,K
result.cublas_bf16_tflops: 1330-1588 (= TK production ceiling ~1540, and reachable via torch.matmul)

verdict: REJECTED. A ThunderKittens tcgen05 GEMM does not beat the vendor path for this campaign's trailing GEMMs. Even TK's production ceiling only ties cuBLAS BF16, which does not beat the shipped TF32 (accuracy-won at 16384) or MXFP8 (3466 TFLOP/s at 32768) trailing. The GEMM is not the bottleneck; the serial diagonal factorization is. Root stays on #913511.
next_action: Lever #3 closed with B200 evidence. No root/Popcorn/leaderboard change. Next untried high-value lever is Ov (per-call overhead, lever #7), the board's clearest steer, not a tensor-core lesson.
